# C8 — Missing Reuse

*Level 1 card. 4 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from failing to store and reuse results of expensive computations, lookups, or data fetches, causing the same work to be repeated across calls, requests, or access sites. This includes not caching deterministic function results for repeated identical inputs (missing memoization), not pre-computing and storing derived artifacts like compiled regex or parsed configs (missing derived-value reuse), not caching chained attribute/scope lookups in local variables in hot code (missing local lookup caching), and repeatedly fetching the same data from external sources when local caching would eliminate the round-trip (redundant data fetching). Distinguished from Redundant Computation (C1) by spanning across calls or access sites rather than within a single scope.

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | Looks for | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C8.S1** | Missing Memoization Cache | a deterministic computation repeated across calls that a cache would answer | cache the result, keyed on the arguments, with a lifetime you have chosen | yes, scales with call count |
| **C8.S2** | Missing Derived-Value Reuse | an expensive artefact derived again on every use instead of once for the process | derive the artefact once and bind it where it survives the calls that use it | yes, scales with call count |
| **C8.S3** | Missing Local Lookup Caching | a name or attribute chain re-resolved every iteration for a value that never moves | bind the resolved value to a local before the hot region | yes, scales with input |
| **C8.S4** | Redundant Data Fetching | the same external data fetched again when the copy in memory was still good | fetch once and reuse, with a lifetime and an invalidation rule you have stated | yes, scales with call count |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C8.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C8.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C8.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C8.S4.md`

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from a category you have already opened is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because something drew you here, which is not the same as a smell being present.
